name: The King's Bedchamber
firstVisit: It's very red in here. It's very gold. It's very him.

W: Black stone, hung with red velvet. The velvet is embroidered with his face, small and repeating, like a wallpaper. It's him. It's all him.
1: The corridor, and his wives' laughter, very faintly, from the far end.
c: A torch. The only thing in here he hasn't put his face on.
f: Portraits of Kaldor, one for every twenty years or so. Five hundred years of them, all down the wall.
He doesn't age a day in any of them. The painters do. You can tell by the brushwork: steady, then shaky, then somebody new.
g: The best chair in the room, turned to face the wall.
There's no dust on the seat, and no dent in the cushion. It's kept ready for someone.
Whoever it's for has never come. It's kept ready anyway.
y: His vanity. Forty pots of something for the face, a comb for the beard, and a smaller comb for the comb.
The mirror's been polished so hard there's a dip in the middle.
Q: The king's bed. Enormous. Black velvet, gold tassels, a hundred pillows.
Not one of them has a dent in it. The sheets have never been turned down.
Either the maids are very, very good, or he doesn't sleep.
Z: A statue of Kaldor, life-size, at his bedside. In case he wants company.
9: A war map, weighted at the corners with daggers.
The wizard kingdom is circled. Then circled again. Then circled so hard the pen's gone through the table.
Across the top, in a big square hand: THE MARCH. TOMORROW.
'Tomorrow' has been crossed out and written in again so many times the paper's gone soft. The last one's in fresh ink.
8: A barrel, full to the brim with gold coin. Then another. Then another.
He ran out of chests a long time ago.
w: Forty identical fur cloaks, and one that's slightly different. He wears that one on special occasions. It's identical.
h: A bearskin rug. Somebody has stitched his face onto the bear. Somebody had to, apparently.

objects.name: Pellam the Valet
lines: You're not supposed to be in here. I'm not supposed to be in here either. Well, I am. That's the whole job.
I turn the bed down every night. Every morning I turn it back up. Nobody's been in it.

answer: Not that I've seen. Thirty years I've been his valet.
Some nights he sits up here. Not in that chair. Never in that chair. On the little stool, facing it.
He talks to it a while. Then he waits. Then he says 'tomorrow', and goes back downstairs.
He said 'my master', and then he looked at me for a very long time, and I've not asked him anything since.
I've barely said anything since. This is the most I've said in years. It's quite nice, actually.
It's always tomorrow. I've packed his campaign trunk eleven thousand times. I've stopped unpacking it.
...This time he had me polish the good helmet, though.
He's never asked for the good helmet.

questions.ask: Thirty years folding sheets for a man who doesn't sleep? Sad.
answer: I prefer to think of it as thirty years of very well-folded sheets.
Would you like to see the corners? ...No. No, you wouldn't. Nobody ever does.

lines: A ledger on a stand, beside the barrels. Every page has one word on it: MORE.
